question.text: The value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\int_{0}^{x^{2}} \cos \left(t^{2}\right) d t}{x \sin x}$ is

solution.text:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\int_{0}^{x^{2}} \cos \left(t^{2}\right) d t}{x \sin x} \quad\left[\frac{0}{0}\text{ form}\right]$
$=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\cos \left(x^{4}\right) \times 2 x}{\sin x+x \cos x} \quad$ [L' Hospital's rule]
$=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2\left[\cos x^{4}-x \sin \left(x^{4}\right) \times 4 x^{3}\right]}{\cos x+\cos x-x \sin x}$
[L' Hospital's rule]
$=\frac{2[\cos 0-0]}{\cos 0+\cos 0-0}=\frac{2}{1+1}=1$
